# Protected parent verification components

The [protected workflow entry point](entrypoint-README.md) selects only reviewed records from protected default-branch source, then uses the [GitHub resolver](github-parent-README.md), [bounded dispatcher](dispatch-README.md) and [semantic consumer](semantic-gate/README.md). The registry is currently empty, production Trusted remains closed, and candidate-branch tests do not establish protected acceptance.

`provenance.py` is a validation-only parser for the exact protected parent-run artifact required before the downstream Evidence gate can inspect its documents. It has no network client, token reader, process launcher, runtime capability, policy resolver, admission call, `Trusted` result, or gate verdict. Its frozen `ProtectedParentDocuments` result contains only the selected `plan.json` and `manifest.json` bytes.

## Candidate branch controls

The [runtime validation workflow](../workflows/evidencehost-runtime-proof.yml) runs the closed transport tests and actual semantic child on Linux without an API token. Its fixed `issue779-protected-parent-controls-<run>-<attempt>` artifact retains the current source capture and bounded command logs. These public-data and ordinary-process controls are a prerequisite of the unchanged solution gate; they do not execute the protected `main` workflow, enroll a reviewed record or issue Trusted admission.

## Inputs and checks

The caller supplies four independent values: bounded UTF-8 JSON bytes for a protected expectation, a projected actual workflow-run response, a projected actual artifact response, and the downloaded ZIP bytes. The expectation schema is `issue779-protected-parent-expectation-v1` and has exactly `repository`, `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `head_sha`, `workflow_path`, `workflow_sha`, `base_sha`, `subject_sha`, `artifact_id`, `artifact_name`, `artifact_sha256`, and `artifact_bytes` plus the schema field. The run projection supplies the same repository/run/attempt/head/workflow/base/subject facts and the actual event; only `push` and `workflow_dispatch` are accepted. The artifact projection supplies repository, run ID, artifact ID/name, expiry and compressed byte count. Unknown fields, duplicate or case-aliased JSON properties, wrong types (including booleans where integers are required), out-of-range identifiers, unsafe workflow paths, unsupported events, expired or mismatched artifacts, and uppercase/malformed digests reject.

The protected expectation is not inferred from the upload. The caller must source it from its protected parent context. The run and artifact projections must independently come from the authenticated parent repository/run and exact artifact metadata; `workflow_sha`, base and subject facts must already have been resolved against the immutable run/source context before projection. Artifact metadata must include GitHub's exact `digest` form, `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`. The parser requires that digest to match both the protected expectation and a fresh SHA-256 of the exact downloaded bytes before opening the ZIP. Missing, null, malformed, or different API digest metadata rejects before archive parsing. This module does not authenticate those sources or establish that the supplied objects came from GitHub or any other protected provider.

Before constructing `ZipFile`, the parser checks the ZIP structure directly from the already-digest-verified bytes: it scans only the fixed maximum EOCD tail, accepts one EOCD ending exactly at EOF, requires a single-disk non-ZIP64 archive with exactly two entries, caps the central directory at 16 KiB, and walks exactly two bounded central headers. Names, extras, comments, local-header offsets, local names, and compressed-data extents are bounded and checked; ZIP64 extra fields and an unaccounted third central record reject before `ZipFile` can allocate per-entry objects. The supported input is therefore a closed, non-split, non-ZIP64 two-file ZIP format, not a general ZIP reader.

After that structural precheck, standard-library ZIP parsing permits exactly two unencrypted regular-file entries named `plan.json` and `manifest.json`, with no directories, links, traversal, absolute or alternate-separator names, duplicate/case-alias names, or other files. The archive is capped at 32 MiB; each selected document at 1 MiB; total expanded bytes at 2 MiB; and member count at two. ZIP CRC/stream completion is checked while reading within the declared bounds. No filename discovery or fallback member is allowed.

## Required downstream order and limits

This preflight only binds expected parent metadata to independently supplied metadata and exact downloaded bytes, then returns two immutable byte strings. It does not parse a repository policy, prove the workflow was protected, validate plan/manifest semantics, verify a producer assertion, create an admission, or call `EvidenceProtectedGate`. A coherent upload and matching hashes cannot authenticate themselves.

The eventual protected consumer must independently resolve the protected plan/policy from its immutable source, verify the exact artifact download and parent run context, parse and cross-check these documents, and only then invoke the existing [`EvidenceProtectedGate`](../../Evidence/ForgeTrust.AppSurface.Evidence.Contracts/EvidenceProtectedGate.cs) with its protected expectation. Do not use `ProtectedParentDocuments` as a gate-pass or `Trusted` signal. These components add no accepted platform or runtime registration. The separately guarded qualification workflow must be reviewed on protected main and supplied an independently reviewed record before genuine protected integration can run.

The data-only tests use small ZIP byte strings and detached JSON projections. They exercise parser rejection order and selection only; they make no authenticated-parent, workflow, admission, policy, or native-acceptance claim.
